Lemma
[Bishop-Gromov for the volume of a ball]

↗ lem:polar-coordinates ↗ lem:model-ball-volume ↗ def:sinh-comparison-function

Let $k\ge 0$ and $R>0$. Let $ ho \ge 0$ be a measurable density on $T_pM$ (thought of as $ ho (v)=|\det d(\exp _p)_v|$, extended by $0$ past the cut time), and put $\Vol (r)=\int _{B(0,r)} ho \, d\mu $. Suppose that in every unit direction $\omega \in S$ the polar density $ u _\omega (t)=t^{n-1} ho (t\omega )$ has non-increasing ratio to the model density, \[ t\ \longmapsto \ rac{ u _\omega (t)}{\sn _k^{n-1}(t)} \quad ext{non-increasing on }(0,R). \] Then for $0<r_1\le r_2<R$ \[ \Vol (r_2)\cdot \Vol B_{H^n_k}(q_k,r_1)\ \le \Vol (r_1)\cdot \Vol B_{H^n_k}(q_k,r_2), \] equivalently $r\mapsto \Vol (r)/\Vol B_{H^n_k}(q_k,r)$ is non-increasing on $(0,R)$.

Proof

\sketch ↗ lem:polar-coordinates ↗ lem:model-ball-volume

Apply the radial Bishop–Gromov inequality direction by direction, extending each radial density by zero after its cut time. Integrating over the unit sphere and using polar coordinates converts the radial integrals into ball volumes. The ratio-of-integrals lemma then gives monotonicity of the quotient by the model ball volume.

□

Theorem
[Bishop-Gromov relative volume comparison]
